I am a woman of 46 years, farming here in the North West with no schooling. This small plot of 0.29 hectares I plant with beans mixed with other crops, as we always do. I have no money for much fertilizer, and beans do not need it like maize does — they feed the soil themselves. I will put a little manure from our goats and sheep, use the seed I saved from last harvest, and my daughters will help me weed. If caterpillars come to eat the pods, I may ask my husband to buy a small bottle of medicine from the agro-dealer in town, but only if the problem is bad.
